name: Interactive Report Messages Requiring Translation
apex: Reference list of ~400 built-in message names (APEXIR.*) and their English text used inside Interactive Report UI, provided so translators know what to translate.
workflow: Developer looks up a message name here, then creates a matching Text Message translation for each target language.
relevance: Pure reference table of Oracle's own UI strings for a component Paddock does not use; nothing to copy for a single-language site.
skip_for_web: Entire page is a translation lookup table, no concept to adapt.

name: Progressive Web App (PWA) Messages Requiring Translation
apex: Reference list of built-in PWA install-prompt and offline-page strings (per OS/browser instructions, offline fallback page HTML) that ship with every APEX-generated PWA.
workflow: Translator edits each PWA message's Text per language; APEX renders the matching one based on client OS/browser detection.
relevance: Paddock is already a PWA via its own Serwist layer with its own install/offline UX; APEX's per-OS install-instructions dialog is a nice pattern but out of scope for the designer itself.
skip_for_web: Translation strings only; Paddock's PWA shell is already built independently.

name: Search and Smart Filters Messages Requiring Translation
apex: Reference list of built-in Faceted Search / Smart Filter UI strings (APEX.FS.*) such as Clear All, Show Chart, %0 results, for translation.
workflow: Same text-message translation workflow applied to the Smart Filters component's fixed labels.
relevance: Reference table for a component's built-in labels; no new structural idea for the designer.
skip_for_web: Translation-only content.

name: Workflow for Translating Messages into Multiple Languages
apex: The four-step process: create a Text Message in the primary language, copy it with an alternate Language and the same Static ID, then edit the Text of the copy.
workflow: Developer authors once in the base language, then copies per target language with the same Static ID to key the lookup.
relevance: Multi-language translation workflow; Paddock runs one language today so there is nothing to adopt.
skip_for_web: Whole page is language-copy mechanics.

name: Text Messages (Shared Component)
apex: A centralized, per-language dictionary of named strings (Static ID to Text) that pages and JavaScript can reference instead of hard-coding text, with optional %0-style positional substitution.
workflow: Developer creates a message once per language under Shared Components > Globalization > Text Messages, then references its Static ID from pages, JS (APEX.LANG.*), or PL/SQL.
relevance: The centralized named-string-with-substitution-tokens idea is generically useful, but Paddock is single-language so a dedicated strings dictionary is not worth building now.
skip_for_web: Only the translation angle is skipped; the underlying named-constant idea already exists informally in code.

name: Text Message Picker (Page Designer)
apex: An inline picker icon that appears next to every text-capable attribute field in Page Designer, letting a developer search and insert a reference to a shared Text Message without leaving the field.
workflow: Developer enables the picker once via toolbar Utilities, then clicks the small icon beside any field to search shared messages and insert one inline, seeing a live preview.
relevance: The pattern of an inline picker icon on any text field to insert/reference a shared value (with live preview) is a reusable designer UX Paddock Developer could copy for inserting shared Lists/snippets into any component's text attributes.
skip_for_web: Skip the translation-search angle; keep only the inline-reference-picker interaction.

name: Copying or Subscribing to Text Messages
apex: Lets a developer copy a text message within the same app (new language + Static ID) or copy/subscribe to one from a different application in the workspace, tracked via Subscribed From / Subscription Status / Subscribers columns.
workflow: Developer searches the Text Messages report, clicks Copy, and either fills in a new language/ID or picks a source app and enables Subscribe to stay linked to a master copy.
relevance: Cross-application shared-component subscription; Paddock Developer manages one site, so there is no second app to copy or subscribe from.
skip_for_web: Entire cross-app subscription mechanic does not apply to a single-site designer.

name: Subscribing to Text Messages
apex: Links a text message to a master copy in another application so it stays in sync; supports Subscribe, Refresh Text Message, and Unsubscribe actions in the component's Subscription region.
workflow: Developer selects a master message to subscribe from, applies, confirms, then can refresh or unsubscribe later as the master changes.
relevance: Same cross-app subscription model as the previous page; not applicable to a single-site designer with no sibling apps.
skip_for_web: No multi-app concept exists in Paddock Developer.

name: Translating Data That Supports List of Values (Dynamic Translations)
apex: A separate translation mechanism for dynamic, query-driven data (e.g. LOV values from a table) rather than fixed message names: a translate-from string, language code, and translate-to string, resolved at runtime via APEX_LANG.LANG.
workflow: Developer defines from/to string pairs per language on the Dynamic Translations page, then calls APEX_LANG.LANG(p_primary_text_string) in SQL/PLSQL to get the localized value.
relevance: Runtime data translation for multilingual LOVs; not needed while Paddock serves one language.
skip_for_web: Whole mechanism is translation-specific.

name: Understanding Supported Globalization Codes
apex: Reference table mapping ~60 Language Names to Language Code, NLS_LANGUAGE, and NLS_TERRITORY, which control default number/date/currency formatting per application language.
workflow: Developer picks an application Globalization language; APEX looks up this table to set NLS_LANGUAGE/NLS_TERRITORY automatically for formatting.
relevance: Locale code lookup table for multilingual number/date formatting; Paddock formats dates itself (venue-local) for one locale.
skip_for_web: Pure reference data.

name: About Best Practices to Improve Performance
apex: Top-level performance guidance: use bind variables for session-state references in SQL/PLSQL, and monitor page rendering time via Workspace Administration dashboards or the APEX_WORKSPACE_ACTIVITY_LOG view.
attributes: bind variable syntax for session state
workflow: Developer writes SQL/PLSQL referencing session state via bind variables instead of string substitution, then checks dashboards for slow pages.
relevance: Bind-variable advice is Oracle-SQL specific; Paddock has no session-state substitution layer. The monitoring half is already covered by the planned Health page and Data workspace.
skip_for_web: Bind-variable guidance does not translate to Next.js/Supabase.

name: Identifying Performance Issues (bottleneck isolation methodology)
apex: A diagnostic method: compare DB response time vs. browser render time to locate the bottleneck, then isolate the time window, biggest DB time consumers, and the offending SQL/page; addresses slow queries with progress bars, blocking duplicate submissions, and APEX collections to cache expensive query results across pagination/filtering.
attributes: compare server time vs render time
APEX collections to cache query results
workflow: Developer narrows a slow-page complaint to server vs. client, then to a specific SQL statement, using debug mode timings; caches expensive repeat queries instead of re-running them per interaction.
relevance: The bottleneck-isolation method (server time vs render time, then narrow to the offending call) and caching-instead-of-refetching pattern are directly reusable diagnostic habits for Paddock's planned Debug panel and Health page.
skip_for_web: Skip the DB-time/SQL-specific parts; keep the isolate-then-narrow methodology and the cache-repeat-query idea.

name: Monitor Activity page (Workspace Administration)
apex: A categorized analytics dashboard on activity logs, organized into named sections: Page Views, Developer Activity, Sessions, Page View Analysis, Environment, Login Attempts, Application Errors, Workspace Schema Reports, Archived Activity, each holding several named reports/charts.
attributes: Developer Activity (By Developer/Bar Chart/Hour/Day/Application/Application Changes/Monthly/Component Utilization)
Sessions (Active Sessions, Bar Chart by Hour)
Page View Analysis (Most Viewed Pages, Monthly Calendar, Usage by Day, Weighted Page Performance)
workflow: Administrator opens Monitor Activity and picks a named report from a grouped list to inspect a specific slice of usage or error data.
relevance: Good template for organizing Paddock's Health page into named sections (traffic, errors, environments, sessions) rather than one flat dump; copy the grouping-by-concern structure, not the Oracle-specific reports.
skip_for_web: Skip Oracle-specific reports (schema tablespace, login attempts by auth scheme); keep the section groupings.

name: App Builder Dashboard report
apex: A workspace-level summary dashboard on the App Builder home showing Applications count, Pages count, Developer Activity (last 2 days), Page Events, Page Count by Application, Most Active Pages, and Native Region Component Utilization.
workflow: Developer clicks Dashboard from the App Builder home to see at-a-glance workspace health and the most-used pages/components.
relevance: Matches the shape Paddock's Data workspace should aim for: counts, recent activity, most-active pages, and component usage at a glance; validates the existing Data workspace direction.
skip_for_web: None; the summary-tile-plus-most-active-list pattern transfers directly.

name: Managing Log Files / Instance Activity Reports
apex: Instance administrators can delete log files and set the retention interval; to keep activity data indefinitely, a batch job must copy records out of the rotating activity log tables into a separate table before they age out.
attributes: batch job to copy log records
workflow: Administrator sets a retention window for log files, and if longer history is needed, schedules a job to archive rows before rotation deletes them.
relevance: Direct warning for Paddock's Health page: raw request/activity logs are ephemeral by design, so anything worth trending over time must be aggregated into a durable table on a schedule, not read live from rotating logs.
skip_for_web: Skip the Oracle two-table rotation detail; keep the retention-window-plus-archival-job principle.

name: About Utilizing Database Reporting
apex: Describes using Oracle Trace/TKPROF, AWR and ASH reports, and the PL/SQL hierarchical profiler to find resource-intensive SQL, plus APEX dictionary views (readable instance-wide with APEX_ADMINISTRATOR_READ_ROLE) for monitoring.
workflow: DBA correlates a slow APEX page to its SQL via V$SESSION client-identifier tagging, then profiles it with AWR/ASH/TKPROF.
relevance: Entirely Oracle-Database-internals tooling (AWR/ASH/TKPROF/hierarchical profiler); Cloudflare Workers and Supabase have no equivalent surface for the designer to expose.
skip_for_web: Whole page is Oracle DB tracing infrastructure.

name: About Database Parameters that Impact Performance
apex: Lists Oracle memory-related init parameters (MEMORY_TARGET, SGA_TARGET, PGA_AGGREGATE_TARGET, SHARED_POOL_SIZE) to review, and recommends gathering statistics on the APEX schema for the cost-based optimizer.
workflow: DBA reviews and sizes these instance parameters when APEX as a whole runs slowly.
relevance: Oracle instance-tuning parameters with no Cloudflare Worker or Supabase analog.
skip_for_web: Entire page is Oracle memory tuning.

name: About Limiting Resources (Database Resource Manager)
apex: Oracle Database Resource Manager lets an admin define tiered CPU/logical-reads profiles (e.g. APEX_HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW) that automatically downgrade or kill a request's resources the longer it runs, preventing one user from starving others.
attributes: automatic profile switching by elapsed time
workflow: Instance administrator defines CPU/time thresholds per profile; the database automatically demotes a long-running call to a lower-CPU profile and can cancel it past a final threshold.
relevance: Tiered automatic throttling of a runaway request is a generically nice idea, but Cloudflare Workers already impose hard CPU-time limits per request rather than tiered profiles, so there is nothing for the designer to configure here.
skip_for_web: Requires Oracle Database Enterprise Edition; no analog in a Workers runtime.

name: About Uploading Static Files to Your Web Server
apex: Recommends serving static files from the web server instead of the database, enabling gzip compression, and sending cache-expiration headers to browsers.
workflow: Developer moves static assets out of the database BLOB storage path and onto the web tier, and configures compression/caching there.
relevance: Standard static-asset best practice that Cloudflare's CDN and Next.js already provide automatically for Paddock; nothing new to design for.
skip_for_web: Already solved by the existing hosting stack.

name: Enabling Logging for an Application (Logging attribute)
apex: A single Yes/No Logging property on the Edit Application Definition page that turns per-page-view activity logging on or off for that application; recommended Off for high-volume apps.
attributes: Application Activity Logging instance setting must allow 'Use Application Setting'
workflow: Developer flips one property per application to start/stop recording every page view for later analysis.
relevance: Simple, copyable pattern: a single per-app (or per-site) toggle to turn detailed activity logging on/off, useful so Paddock's Health/Debug logging can be switched off cheaply if it ever adds overhead.
skip_for_web: None; the toggle-and-tradeoff framing applies directly.

name: APEX_ACTIVITY_LOG (view schema)
apex: A queryable view recording every logged page view with timestamp, elapsed time, row counts, user/session/IP/user-agent, application and page IDs, and any SQL error message; only the first entry per session stores IP/user-agent to save space.
workflow: Developer queries APEX_ACTIVITY_LOG directly (e.g. via SQL Developer) to build custom per-app monitoring reports, such as page-view counts and average elapsed time grouped by user over the last 24 hours.
relevance: Good reference column set for the request/activity log table behind Paddock's Health page: timestamp, elapsed time, route/page id, user/session, user-agent, and error message are the right fields to capture per request.
skip_for_web: Skip Oracle-specific fields (ir_report_id, component_type/name marked 'reserved for future use'); keep timestamp/elapsed/route/user/error columns.

name: Reviewing Session State (Developer Toolbar > Session)
apex: A Session link on the runtime Developer Toolbar that opens a live report of the current user's session-state values (item names and values) as the app is being used.
workflow: Developer runs the app, clicks Session on the toolbar, and inspects live item values to explain conditional UI behavior.
relevance: Direct precedent for Paddock's planned Debug panel: a toolbar link that surfaces live internal state (route params, fetched data, feature flags) while previewing a page.
skip_for_web: None; the live-state-inspector-in-the-toolbar idea transfers directly.

name: Utilizing Debug Mode (overview)
apex: Umbrella topic for APEX's whole debugging system: a per-application on/off switch, seven cumulative severity levels, runtime toolbar control, remote per-session control, URL-parameter control, instance-wide override, a viewer for captured messages, and a code-level logging API.
workflow: Developer chains these pieces together: enable at the right scope, choose a level, reproduce, then inspect captured messages.
relevance: Good checklist of the pieces a complete Debug panel needs (scope of enablement, verbosity, live control, remote control, a message viewer, and an instrumentation API); use as a coverage checklist rather than copying any one piece verbatim.
skip_for_web: Skip nothing structurally; each sub-piece is scored individually below.

name: Enabling and Disabling Debug Mode for an Application (Debugging attribute)
apex: A Yes/No Debugging property on the Application Definition controlling whether ANY end user can trigger debug mode in the browser at runtime; developers signed into the workspace can always debug regardless of this setting, and it can also be forced on programmatically.
workflow: Developer sets Debugging=No before going to production so the public cannot see internal trace detail, while retaining the ability to debug themselves when signed in.
relevance: Security-conscious pattern worth copying literally: separate 'can developers/admins always debug' from 'can the public trigger debug mode', defaulting the public path to off in production.
skip_for_web: None.

name: Available Debug Levels
apex: Seven cumulative severity levels for debug logging: Error(1), Warn(2), Info(4, default), Application Enter(5), Application Trace(6), APEX Engine Enter(8), APEX Engine Trace(9, includes SQL execution plans); each higher level includes all lower ones and costs more performance.
workflow: Developer picks the lowest level that shows the needed detail; Oracle recommends staying at Application Trace or below unless directed otherwise.
relevance: Reusable verbosity model for the Debug panel: split levels along two axes (severity, and your-code vs framework-internals) and warn that deeper levels cost performance and should not be default.
skip_for_web: Collapse from 7 raw levels to a small curated set in the UI, as APEX itself does on its own toolbar (see next entry).

name: Controlling Debug Mode for a Page at Runtime (Developer Toolbar > Debug)
apex: A Debug menu on the runtime Developer Toolbar with exactly four curated choices (Off, Info default, App Trace, Full Trace) mapped onto the seven raw levels, plus a separate View Debug action that opens the captured report for the current page; the chosen mode persists as long as the browser tab stays open.
workflow: Developer picks a verbosity from a 4-item toolbar menu, reproduces the issue, then clicks View Debug to inspect what was captured for that page.
relevance: Directly copyable UX for Paddock's preview-toolbar Debug panel: expose a small 4-option menu (Off/Info/Trace/Full) rather than raw levels, plus a one-click 'View Debug' to see what was captured for the current page.
skip_for_web: None; this is the cleanest precedent found so far for the panel's own control surface.

name: Configuring Debug Mode Using the Session Detail Report
apex: An admin can open any active session's Session Detail report (Monitor Activity > Active Sessions) and set its Debug Level and Trace Mode remotely, turning on tracing for a session that is not their own.
workflow: Admin finds another user's live session in a list, opens its detail report, and raises its debug level so the next requests from that user get captured.
relevance: Valuable capability for a two-person team supporting real users: let an admin flip on tracing for one specific live visitor/session from the Health page without needing that visitor to do anything.
skip_for_web: None; the remote-enable-for-one-session idea is the core value.

name: Configuring the Debug Level Programmatically (APEX_SESSION.SET_DEBUG)
apex: A PL/SQL API call that sets the debug level for all future requests in the current session, an alternative to the toolbar or Session Detail report.
workflow: Developer calls the API once in code to persist a debug level across a session's remaining requests.
relevance: Just a programmatic equivalent of the toolbar toggle already captured; no new UI concept for the designer.
skip_for_web: API-only restatement of an already-captured concept.

name: Using URL Parameters to Control Debug Mode
apex: A debug query parameter (?debug=YES or ?debug=LEVELn, n = 1/2/4/5/6/8/9) on either Friendly URL or f?p syntax that forces a given page load into debug mode without touching the toolbar; error messages are always logged even when debug mode is off.
workflow: Developer appends a query parameter to a specific link to force that one request into debug mode, e.g. to share a reproducible debug URL.
relevance: A shareable ?debug= URL parameter is a low-effort way to force Paddock's Debug panel on for one request/link, useful for the two-person team handing off a repro link; also confirms errors should always log regardless of debug state.
skip_for_web: None.

name: Controlling the Debug Level for an Instance (SYSTEM_DEBUG_LEVEL)
apex: An instance administrator API (APEX_INSTANCE_ADMIN.SET_PARAMETER with SYSTEM_DEBUG_LEVEL) that overrides the default debug level for the entire hosted instance; strongly recommended only for short periods due to the performance hit.
workflow: Admin temporarily raises debug verbosity for the whole instance to catch an issue, then resets it to NULL immediately after.
relevance: Confirms a global emergency override belongs at the top of the admin hierarchy above per-app and per-session controls, with an explicit 'use briefly then turn off' warning worth echoing in Paddock's own Health/Debug settings.
skip_for_web: None.

name: Debug Report with step timing graph (Viewing Debug Messages for an Application)
apex: Clicking View Debug opens a report listing debug sessions; opening one shows a bar graph of steps above the message list, where hovering a bar shows that step's timing detail and clicking it jumps the report to that step. Debug sessions are retained at least 2 weeks alongside the activity log.
attributes: click bar to jump to step
workflow: Developer opens View Debug, picks a session, then visually spots the slowest bar on the graph and clicks it to jump straight to that step's messages.
relevance: Strong, concrete UX idea for Paddock's Debug panel: a per-request timeline/bar chart of steps where hovering shows duration and clicking jumps to that step's detail, rather than a flat scrollable log.
skip_for_web: None; this is one of the standout transferable patterns in the whole debugging chapter.

name: Debug Messages page in Utilities (view/purge)
apex: A persistent Utilities page listing all debug messages for an application (not just the current toolbar session) with a Purge Debug Messages action offering four scopes: all messages, messages older than N days/weeks, current session only, or by a specific View Identifier.
workflow: Developer opens Utilities > Debug Messages to browse historical captures, then purges old or unwanted entries by age, session, or specific ID.
relevance: Good reusable set of purge/retention controls for a Debug or Health log screen: purge-all, purge-by-age, purge-current-only, and purge-by-id cover the realistic cleanup needs without over-building.
skip_for_web: None.

name: Querying Debug Messages (APEX_WORKSPACE_ACTIVITY_LOG to APEX_DEBUG_MESSAGES correlation)
apex: Debug messages are correlated to a specific request via a DEBUG_PAGE_VIEW_ID: look it up in APEX_WORKSPACE_ACTIVITY_LOG by application/page/timestamp, then query APEX_DEBUG_MESSAGES filtered to that page_view_id for the ordered message trail.
workflow: Developer finds the row for the slow/erroring request in the activity log, notes its page-view id, then pulls every debug message for that exact id in order.
relevance: The correlation-id pattern (one id linking an activity-log row to its full detailed trace) is exactly the join Paddock's Health page needs between a request/activity entry and its Debug panel trace.
skip_for_web: Skip the raw-SQL mechanics; keep the correlation-id design.

name: Available Debug Utility Scripts (SQL*Plus scripts: activity/d0/d1/d2/ds)
apex: SYSDBA-only CLI scripts for environments without App Builder access: d0 toggles instance debug fully on/off, d1 lists the last 30 traced requests, ds filters that list to one APEX session, and d2 dumps one PAGE_VIEW_ID's full message detail to a file.
workflow: DBA toggles global trace on, reproduces the bug, toggles it off, lists recent traced requests, narrows to one, and dumps its detail to a text file for review.
relevance: The toggle-then-reproduce-then-list-then-drill-into-one workflow is sound but the delivery is raw SQL*Plus scripts requiring SYSDBA; Paddock's admin surface is a web UI, so only the underlying workflow (already captured elsewhere) transfers, not this tooling.
skip_for_web: Entire CLI/SYSDBA mechanism.

name: Debugging an APEX Session from the User Interface (remote live-session trace + Page View Type + Call Stack)
apex: For environments without SYSDBA access: create a temporary public page, find the affected user's Active Session in Monitor Activity, set its Debug Level to APEX Trace, have them reproduce the error, then open that session's Page View list and click the Debug ID for the failing request; the report can add a Call Stack column, and requests are typed as Rendering, Processing, or AJAX (modal dialogs are separate page numbers).
attributes: Page View Type: Rendering / Processing / AJAX
workflow: Admin remotely arms tracing on a real user's session, has them reproduce the bug, then opens the specific failing request's debug detail by its Debug ID, adding Call Stack for depth.
relevance: The three-way Page View Type split (render vs. submit vs. partial/AJAX) is a clean way to categorize log entries in a Debug panel or Health log so a developer picks the right instance instead of scanning a flat list.
skip_for_web: Skip the public-page workaround and Call Stack column (no SYSDBA-free gap exists in Paddock's own architecture); keep the Page View Type categorization.

name: Tips for Sharing Debug Output
apex: Best practices for capturing a debug trace to hand off (e.g. to Oracle Support or a teammate): pick the minimum level that shows the issue, add the Call Stack column at deep levels, choose the correct Page View ID for the operation's phase (render/submit/AJAX), and export the report as HTML or Excel for offline review (or via the d2.sql script if no App Builder access).
attributes: correct Page View ID by phase
workflow: Developer captures a trace at the right verbosity, picks the exact request instance, and downloads it as HTML/Excel to attach to a bug report.
relevance: For a two-person team, an export/download action on a captured debug trace (HTML or JSON file) is a practical, low-cost addition so one person can hand a repro to the other without shared live access.
skip_for_web: Skip the Oracle Support-specific advice; keep the export-for-handoff feature.

name: Using APEX_DEBUG When Developing Your Application
apex: A developer-facing logging API (APEX_DEBUG.ERROR/WARN/INFO/ENTER/TRACE/MESSAGE/LOG_LONG_MESSAGE in PL/SQL, plus apex.debug in JavaScript) that lets custom application code add its own messages into the same unified debug log the framework already writes to, gated by the same session/instance debug level, with a client-side variant that only prints to the browser console when debug is active.
workflow: Developer sprinkles APEX_DEBUG.* calls in PL/SQL and apex.debug calls in JS; both stay silent unless the session's debug level is high enough, then appear interleaved with framework messages in the same viewer.
relevance: The most actionable idea in this chapter: give Paddock's own component/template authors a small server + client debug-logging helper that feeds the same unified Debug panel timeline as the framework's own instrumentation, gated by the same on/off/level switch.
skip_for_web: None; this is a top finding to carry into the Debug panel plan.

name: Removing Controls and Components to Isolate a Problem (Comment Out / Uncomment)
apex: A right-click 'Comment Out' / 'Uncomment' context menu on any component in Page Designer's Rendering, Dynamic Actions, or Processing tabs that excludes it from runtime (backed by a build option named Commented Out) without deleting it, to binary-search which component causes a bug; a Server-side Condition of Never is the alternative but destroys any existing condition.
attributes: Page Designer context menu: Comment Out
Server-side Condition = Never (destructive to existing condition)
workflow: Developer right-clicks a suspect component, comments it out, reloads the page, and repeats across components until the bug disappears, then uncomments the innocent ones.
relevance: Directly copyable for Paddock Developer's component tree/canvas: a non-destructive 'disable this component at runtime' toggle (flag, not delete) for binary-search debugging, distinct from permanently deleting or hiding it.
skip_for_web: None; strong, simple, high-value pattern.

name: About Monitoring Application and Page Resource Use
apex: APEX tags each database session's module via DBMS_APPLICATION_INFO with the app ID and page number so an admin can query V$SESSION and V$SQLAREA to see which pages are consuming resources.
attributes: module = APEX + app id + page number
workflow: DBA queries these views filtered by the APEX module tag to attribute database load back to a specific application page.
relevance: Oracle session-view tagging with no Cloudflare Worker/Supabase equivalent; request attribution in Paddock would come from its own request logging, not a shared DB session table.
skip_for_web: Entire mechanism is Oracle-session-specific.

name: Enabling SQL Tracing and Using TKPROF
apex: Enable a per-request SQL trace file via the p_trace=YES f?p argument, then analyze it offline with the operating-system TKPROF utility to see execution plans and timings for every SQL statement in that page request.
attributes: tkprof command-line utility (waits, sort, print, aggregate, explain, etc. options)
workflow: Developer loads a page with the trace flag set, locates the resulting trace file on the DB server, and runs tkprof on it to get a readable SQL performance report.
relevance: Oracle SQL-trace/TKPROF tooling has no counterpart in a Cloudflare Worker + Supabase (Postgres) stack; Supabase's own query tooling would be the analog, not something the designer exposes.
skip_for_web: Entire page is Oracle DB trace tooling.

name: Running Advisor to Check Application Integrity
apex: Advisor is a lint/compiler-style checker that scans an application's (or a single page's) metadata for errors, security issues, performance bottlenecks, accessibility problems, and other quality-assurance issues; a Checks to Perform list lets you pick which rule categories run, results are filterable, and it is meant to be re-run after fixes.
workflow: Developer opens Advisor, picks which checks matter, runs it against all or specific pages, reviews a filterable results list, fixes issues, and re-runs to confirm they are gone.
relevance: Strong candidate for Paddock's Health page beyond analytics: a one-click, filterable, re-runnable integrity/quality audit (broken references, accessibility gaps, missing required settings) across the whole site or one page.
skip_for_web: Skip Oracle-specific checks; keep the run-checks/filter-results/re-run-to-verify pattern.

name: System Development Life Cycle Methodologies (Waterfall/Spiral/RAD)
apex: General software-engineering background on Waterfall, Spiral, and Rapid Application Development methodologies, noting APEX's wizard-driven prototyping fits Spiral/RAD better than Waterfall.
workflow: Not tool-specific; informs how a team plans iterations rather than any screen or setting.
relevance: Generic project-methodology theory, not a designer feature; Paddock's branch-PR-merge loop is already an iterative/RAD-style process.
skip_for_web: Whole page is process theory with no UI counterpart.

name: Suggested Environments and Deployment Scenarios
apex: Recommends three environments (development, runtime-only test, runtime-only production) so only DBAs touch test/prod, deployed via export/import across same-or-different workspace/schema/database combinations; recommends never hard-coding an application ID, using an alias or APP_ID/APP_ALIAS substitution strings instead.
attributes: runtime-only environment (no App Builder/SQL Workshop access)
export/import across workspace, schema, or database
workflow: Developer builds only in dev; DBA exports and imports into locked-down test/production environments using APIs or SQLcl, never hand-editing there.
relevance: Paddock already runs an equivalent three-branch/three-Worker topology (documented in CONTRIBUTING.md) with previews sharing prod data and only main deploying; the never-hard-code-the-id principle is already followed via env vars.
skip_for_web: Environment topology already solved differently (git branches, not export files).

name: Export/Import overview and APEXlang format
apex: Exporting creates either a SQL script (.sql) or an APEXlang ZIP (human-readable, modifiable, named APPLICATION-ALIAS.ZIP) explicitly described as optimized for AI generation, human readability, and source-control systems; import can happen immediately or be deferred via the Export Repository, and applications should be imported before related files.
workflow: Developer exports in APEXlang format when the artifact is meant to be diffed/reviewed/committed, or SQL when it just needs to run somewhere.
relevance: Directly validates Paddock's own weekly design-export-to-git-branch plan: Oracle itself introduced a format specifically for git-friendliness and AI/human readability, confirming that a plain SQL/JSON dump is the wrong shape for a diffable export and a structured per-component format is the right one.
skip_for_web: None; treat APEXlang's stated goals as the bar for Paddock's own export format.

name: Splitting Export Files into Separate SQL Scripts (per-component files for version control)
apex: Split Into Multiple Files / Export as Zip options break one big export into one file per page/component so a version-control commit touches only what actually changed, named deterministically by app id, page number, or component name (special characters stripped, spaces to underscores); shared set_environment.sql/end_environment.sql bracket files hoist common setup/teardown out of each per-file script for performance.
attributes: component files named from the component's App Builder name
workflow: Developer splits the export so each commit's diff shows only the pages/components actually touched, instead of one opaque whole-app file.
relevance: This is the exact shape Paddock's weekly git export should take: one file per page/component so a reviewer's diff is scoped to what changed, not a full-app dump; also copy the shared setup/teardown-file idea if the export needs any cross-file bootstrap.
skip_for_web: Skip Oracle's SQL-script naming mechanics; keep the one-file-per-component-for-clean-diffs principle.

name: Component rename breaks export file identity (landmine)
apex: Component export file names are derived from the component's current name in App Builder; renaming a component (e.g. a breadcrumb from 'Menu' to 'Main Menu') changes its exported file name on the next export (menu.sql to main_menu.sql), and the developer is responsible for manually git-mv'ing the old file to preserve history since APEX does not track the rename itself.
attributes: export file name derived from component name
no automatic rename tracking across exports
workflow: Developer renames a component, then must manually rename/move the corresponding file in their version-control checkout to avoid orphaning history.
relevance: Concrete landmine for Paddock's own weekly git export: if exported file names are derived from a component's display name/slug, renaming a component in the designer will silently orphan the old file's git history on the next automated export unless the export logic keys files by a stable internal ID instead of the current name.
skip_for_web: None; this is an actionable warning, not a feature to build.

name: About Exporting Static Files
apex: Static application/workspace files (images, CSS, other binary assets stored in the database) need a separate export path from component SQL scripts: either a ZIP download from Shared Components, or bundled via a Component Export's installation scripts.
attributes: Shared Components static file ZIP download
Component Export installation scripts for static files
workflow: Developer exports binary static assets separately from the structural/metadata export since they do not fit a SQL script format.
relevance: Paddock does not store static assets inside its database the way APEX does (DB BLOBs); assets already live in the repo or R2, so there is no equivalent binary-vs-metadata export split to design.
skip_for_web: Only relevant to APEX's DB-stored file model.

name: Export Type: Standard / Runtime / Full / Custom Export
apex: Four export profiles bundling different scope: Standard (source-control default: dev comments+audit, no runtime/report-settings data), Runtime (for test/prod: strips comments/audit/runtime data, forces Run-Application-Only build status), Full (everything including live runtime data like workflow/task instances, explicitly NOT recommended for source control since it carries environment-specific data), and Custom (pick every option individually).
attributes: Type: Standard Export (default, for source control)
Type: Full Export (migration, not for source control)
workflow: Developer picks Standard when committing to version control, Runtime when pushing to a locked-down environment, Full only when migrating everything including live data, Custom to fine-tune.
relevance: The Standard-vs-Full split is the key design decision for Paddock's weekly git export: it must ship the equivalent of 'Standard' (structure/definition/comments only) and explicitly exclude anything resembling live runtime/analytics data, never a 'Full' dump, to keep the git history meaningful and avoid leaking user data.
skip_for_web: Skip the Runtime build-status-lock mechanic (no comparable 'lock this copy to run-only' concept in Paddock); keep the Standard-vs-Full scoping distinction.

name: Original IDs (export ID stability for diff-friendly version control)
apex: A Custom Export toggle that, when On, keeps each component's exported ID as of the last import rather than its current internal ID, explicitly to minimize spurious changes in version-controlled export files, ease comparison between versions, and keep shared-component subscriptions linked correctly.
attributes: Original IDs: On (IDs as of last import)
use case: readable diffs across versions
use case: keep Shared Component Subscriptions linked
workflow: Developer enables Original IDs before exporting to version control so re-exporting an unchanged component produces an identical (or minimally different) file rather than a full rewrite from regenerated IDs.
relevance: Critical, directly actionable lesson for Paddock's weekly automated export: component identifiers in the exported files must be stable/deterministic across runs, or every weekly export will show every component as changed even when nothing was edited, making the git history useless for review.
skip_for_web: None; this is one of the most important findings in the whole deploying chapter.

name: Custom Export granular inclusion toggles (reports, translations, debugging, workflow/task instances, audit info)
apex: A set of independent On/Off export options separating the application's structural definition from environment- or user-specific state: Public Reports, Private Reports, Report Subscriptions, Comments, Translations, Debugging (enabled/disabled in the exported copy), Workflow Instances, Task Instances, and an Audit Information level (None / Names and Dates / Dates Only).
attributes: Audit Information: None/Names and Dates/Dates Only
workflow: Developer decides per export which categories of user-generated or environment-specific state should ride along with the structural definition.
relevance: General principle Paddock's export should follow: give the export a clear line between 'design/structure' (always exported) and 'live/user state' (never exported to git), rather than one all-or-nothing dump.
skip_for_web: Skip the individual Oracle-specific categories (workflow/task instances, IR subscriptions); keep the structure-vs-state separation principle.

name: Build Status Override (Run Application Only vs Run and Build Application)
apex: An export-time setting that can lock the exported copy so it can only be run, not edited (Run Application Only), as a way to protect an environment from developer changes; changing it back later requires APEX Administration Services (Web import UI only, not command line).
attributes: Build Status Override: Run Application Only
Build Status Override: Run and Build Application
p_trace cannot be set to Yes under Run Application Only
workflow: Developer exports a locked, run-only copy for an environment where only DBAs/admins should be able to re-enable editing.
relevance: Paddock already enforces this via its own mechanism (isProductionWorker()/PADDOCK_ENV gating design writes to prod, and previews vs main), so a separate exported-copy lock state is redundant with the existing environment gate.
skip_for_web: Redundant with Paddock's existing production write-gate.

name: Owner Override and 'As of' point-in-time export (DBMS_FLASHBACK)
apex: Owner Override lets an export be imported under a different schema owner than it was exported from. 'As of' lets a developer export the application as it existed N minutes in the past (via DBMS_FLASHBACK, limited by UNDO_RETENTION, typically ~3 hours), useful for recovering a recently deleted object.
workflow: Developer sets 'As of' to a few minutes before an accidental deletion to export and recover the prior state of the application.
relevance: Paddock's weekly export to a git branch already gives equivalent (and longer-lived) point-in-time recovery for free via git history, so no dedicated flashback-export feature is needed; Owner Override has no schema-owner equivalent in Supabase.
skip_for_web: Git history already solves the 'recover a recent version' need this feature exists for.

name: Exporting a Single Application Page (cross-system ID-match warning + in-editor export entry point)
apex: Single-page export/import across systems only works if both systems share the same application ID, workspace ID, and Shared Component IDs, and any new/updated Shared Components the page references must be exported and imported first or the import fails; a page can be exported either from the standalone Export page or as a quick action from Page Designer's own Utilities menu.
attributes: cross-system requirement: same Shared Component IDs
dependency ordering: shared components before the page
workflow: Developer exports/imports shared components a page depends on before exporting the page itself, or simply uses Page Designer's own Export action while already editing that page.
relevance: Two takeaways: (1) landmine for any future per-page/partial export in Paddock Developer — cross-references to shared components (Lists, Component Settings) must resolve or a partial import breaks; (2) the in-editor 'export just this page' quick action is a nice convenience UX to mirror alongside a broader export/Data screen.
skip_for_web: Skip the exact-ID-match requirement mechanics (Paddock's git-based export does not need cross-instance ID matching); keep the dependency-ordering warning and the in-editor export entry point.

name: Exporting Application Components (cherry-pick + backup-before-editing + Include Installation Files Off for VCS)
apex: A Components export lets a developer search and add specific shared/page components to a 'Components to Export' staging list (reviewable and editable before committing), explicitly framed as either a pre-edit backup or a patch for another instance; a ZIP export's 'Include Installation Files' should be turned Off when saving to version control so boilerplate install/set_environment/end_environment files are not needlessly rewritten.
attributes: Components to Export region (removable before export)
workflow: Developer searches for one or more specific components, adds them to a staging list, reviews it, then exports just that subset either as a quick backup before a risky edit or as a targeted patch.
relevance: Two reusable ideas: a search-and-stage picker for selecting exactly which components to include in an export/snapshot, and the git-hygiene lesson that boilerplate/scaffold files should be excluded from version-controlled exports so they do not churn on every run without real changes.
skip_for_web: Skip the Oracle installation-script specifics; keep the cherry-pick staging UI and the exclude-boilerplate-from-VCS principle.

name: Unified Export page with per-artifact-type tabs (Themes, Plug-ins, and others)
apex: A single Export page under Workspace Utilities holds one tab per exportable artifact type (Application, Page, Components, Themes, Plug-ins, UI Defaults, Feedback, Catalog, Workspace), each tab exposing the same few common fields (format, audit information, file character set) alongside type-specific ones; most artifact-specific export pages (Themes, Plug-ins, Team Development Feedback, REST Source Catalog, Workspace, Script Repository) are also reachable as a shortcut from that artifact's own management page.
attributes: common fields: Audit Information, File Character Set
shortcut entry point from each artifact's own page (e.g. Tasks > Export)
workflow: Developer opens one central Export page and switches tabs by artifact type, or jumps to Export directly from whichever artifact they are already managing.
relevance: Good structural template for Paddock's Data/export workspace: one central export hub organized by artifact type (pages, components, lists, settings) with a consistent set of common options, plus a shortcut from each item's own screen, rather than scattered one-off export buttons.
skip_for_web: Skip the Oracle-specific artifact types (UI Defaults, Team Development Feedback, REST Source Catalog, Workspace-level export) that have no Paddock equivalent; keep the hub-with-tabs-plus-shortcuts structure.

name: Exporting Plug-ins, UI Defaults, Team Development Feedback, REST Source Catalog, Workspace, and Script Repository files
apex: Six more Export-page tabs/utilities for artifact types specific to Oracle APEX's multi-tenant workspace model: Plug-ins (reusable component code), UI Defaults (schema-driven Table/Attribute Dictionary defaults for auto-generated forms), Team Development Feedback (user feedback threads, with a 'Changes Since' date filter), REST Source Catalogs, whole Workspaces (users, groups, SQL history, Minimal vs Full scope), and saved Script Repository files.
attributes: UI Defaults: Table Dictionary vs Attribute Dictionary
Feedback export: Changes Since date filter
Workspace export: Include Team Development, Include Extension Links, Export Type Minimal/Full
workflow: Developer picks the matching Export tab for whichever artifact type needs to move to another instance.
relevance: Each is either an Oracle multi-tenant-workspace concept (users/groups/SQL history) or schema-driven form-generation metadata that Paddock's single-tenant, component-based site has no equivalent for; the shared hub/tab pattern they confirm is already captured.
skip_for_web: None of the six artifact types map onto anything Paddock Developer manages.

name: Exporting UI Defaults
apex: Exports the Table Dictionary (per schema/table/column) and Attribute Dictionary (per column name/synonym) that auto-populate initial region/item property values for schema-driven forms and reports, from either the Export page or the standalone UI Defaults page (with DOS/UNIX line-ending choice).
workflow: Developer exports schema-derived form/report defaults so a target instance's wizards produce the same initial labels/settings for matching tables and columns.
relevance: Paddock's designer is not a schema-driven auto-form generator over arbitrary database tables, so there is no Table/Attribute Dictionary equivalent to export.
skip_for_web: Entire concept depends on schema-driven form generation, which Paddock does not do.

name: Exporting Team Development Feedback
apex: Exports user-submitted feedback threads (with an optional 'Changes Since' date filter) so they can be migrated into another instance's Team Development feedback tracker.
workflow: Developer exports only feedback submitted after a chosen date to move recent items to another instance.
relevance: Team Development's feedback tracker has no Paddock equivalent; covered structurally by the unified Export-hub entry already recorded.
skip_for_web: No feedback-tracker feature exists in Paddock Developer.

name: Exporting a REST Source Catalog
apex: Exports a REST Source Catalog definition (a set of reusable REST data source templates) as a SQL script for import into another instance.
attributes: Export Catalog task shortcut from REST Source Catalogs page
workflow: Developer exports a REST Source Catalog to replicate a set of reusable REST endpoint templates elsewhere.
relevance: REST Source Catalogs are an Oracle-specific reusable-connector library; Paddock's data-source connections are code (lib/results/*, lib/standings/*), not a catalog artifact type to export.
skip_for_web: No catalog-of-REST-sources concept exists in Paddock.

name: Exporting a Workspace
apex: Exports an entire multi-tenant Workspace (users, groups, Team Development data, SQL Scripts/history, saved SQL, user preferences, login history, email logs, UI Defaults) as one script, scoped Minimal (default) or Full; does not include applications and is only recommended when migrating workspace users or shared-component subscriptions.
workflow: An instance admin exports a whole workspace to replicate its user base and shared-component subscription graph on another instance, separately from any application.
relevance: Paddock has no multi-tenant workspace-of-developers concept to migrate; it is a single site with one repo and one Supabase project.
skip_for_web: Entire concept is Oracle's multi-tenant workspace model.

name: Exporting Script Files from the Script Repository
apex: A stub topic pointing to the SQL Workshop guide for moving saved SQL scripts out of a workspace's Script Repository.
workflow: Developer exports saved ad hoc SQL scripts to move them to another workspace.
relevance: Paddock has no in-browser saved-SQL-scripts feature; database work happens in code/migrations.
skip_for_web: No equivalent feature exists.

name: Importing Export Files (general flow: upload, defer, version rule, ordering)
apex: A single Import page accepts drag-and-drop upload of any export file type, offers immediate import or deferred import later from the Export Repository, enforces that an application cannot be imported into an earlier APEX release than it was exported from, and recommends always importing the application before its related files.
attributes: immediate import vs. deferred via Export Repository
import order: application before related files
workflow: Developer uploads a file, picks its type, either imports now or parks it in the Export Repository, respecting version and ordering constraints.
relevance: Two portable rules for any future import/apply-from-git-branch feature: enforce forward-only compatibility (reject an export made by a newer designer schema) and always apply in a fixed dependency order (shared building blocks before the pages that reference them).
skip_for_web: Skip the file-upload mechanics; keep the two compatibility/ordering rules.

name: Import As Application ID handling + locked-application import block
apex: On import, a developer chooses Auto Assign New Application ID, Reuse Application ID (destructively deletes and replaces any existing app with that ID in the target), or Change Application ID (must be unique instance-wide); importing into an application currently locked by another user is blocked outright with a notification page.
attributes: import blocked when target app is locked by another user
workflow: Developer picks how the incoming app's identity maps onto the target instance, and is stopped cold if someone else currently has the target app locked for editing.
relevance: The lock-blocks-import rule is a concurrency-safety pattern worth copying for Paddock: an apply-from-git-branch action (or any bulk write) should refuse to run while another editor has an active session/lock on the affected page, rather than silently overwriting their in-progress work.
skip_for_web: Skip the application-ID-reuse mechanics (Paddock has no equivalent numeric app-ID identity to reassign).

name: Subscription Mode on import + post-import dependency wizard + confirmation landing actions
apex: When an import contains subscribed components, a Subscription Mode (Strict, Ignore Errors, Remove, or Legacy) controls how mismatches against the target's own subscription state are handled; after import, the wizard detects and walks through provisioning any Credentials, Remote Servers, or Supporting Objects the imported content needs; a final confirmation page offers Upgrade/Edit/Run Application shortcuts.
workflow: Developer imports a file, resolves any subscription conflicts by mode, is guided through provisioning any missing external dependencies the import needs, then jumps straight into editing or running from the confirmation page.
relevance: The detect-missing-dependencies-and-walk-through-provisioning-them pattern is a good model for a future Paddock import/apply flow: if an incoming branch's design references a data source, secret, or component the current environment lacks, surface and help fill that gap immediately rather than failing silently.
skip_for_web: Skip the subscription-conflict-mode specifics (no cross-app subscription concept in Paddock).

name: Atomic transactional component install (delete-then-install, all-or-nothing rollback)
apex: Installing components from an import file first deletes the existing matching components, then installs the new ones; if every statement succeeds the whole install commits permanently, but if any error occurs the entire install rolls back leaving no permanent changes at all. Importing a page or component that references a shared component or table missing from the target raises an error, so dependencies must be imported first.
attributes: Confirm Replace Page / Confirm Components replace prompt
missing-dependency error if a referenced shared component/table is absent
workflow: Developer imports a component file; the system either fully replaces the old components with the new ones or, on any failure, leaves the application completely untouched.
relevance: Directly actionable reliability requirement for any future Paddock import/apply-from-git-branch operation: make the apply atomic (fully succeed or fully roll back), never leave the live site in a half-applied state; and validate all referenced shared components exist before starting.
skip_for_web: None; this is one of the strongest, most concrete findings in the deploying chapter.

name: Re-importing an Application Containing Background Processes
apex: Redeploying over an application that has scheduled/background page processes warns if executions are running or waiting, and offers Disable Background Execution (sets Maximum Scheduler Jobs to zero, blocking new runs, without installing yet) or Replace Application (installs immediately, terminating running executions and deleting waiting ones).
attributes: Disable Background Execution (drain, no install yet)
Replace Application (force install, kills running + waiting executions)
workflow: Developer sees a warning before redeploying over an app with live scheduled jobs, and chooses to either pause new runs first (drain) or force the replace immediately and accept in-flight work is lost.
relevance: Directly relevant to Paddock's own scheduled work (warm-live-data loader runs, publish cron): any future 'apply this design change' action should warn if it could disrupt an in-flight loader/cron run and offer the same drain-first-or-force-now choice rather than silently interrupting it.
skip_for_web: Skip the Maximum-Scheduler-Jobs mechanic; keep the warn-and-choose-drain-or-force pattern.

name: About Importing Applications and Application Groups
apex: On import, an application's group membership resolves by matching group ID first, then group name, then creating a new group as a last resort (reusing the exported group ID if free, otherwise generating a new one).
workflow: Developer imports an app; APEX silently resolves which application group it lands in on the target instance using this fallback chain.
relevance: Application Groups organize multiple apps within one workspace; Paddock is a single site with no multi-app grouping concept.
skip_for_web: No equivalent multi-app organizational feature exists.

name: Importing Themes, Plug-ins, UI Defaults, Team Development Feedback, REST Source Catalog
apex: Each follows the same Import-page pattern (file type selector, target application, optional Subscription Mode) with minor type-specific behavior: Theme and Plug-in installs are atomic (rollback on any error) and blocked on a locked target app; a Plug-in import overwrites any existing plug-in of the same name; UI Defaults Table Dictionary import fully overwrites while Attribute Dictionary import merges (replacing matches, keeping non-matching entries).
attributes: atomic install with rollback (Theme, Plug-in, UI Defaults)
Plug-in import overwrites by matching name
Attribute Dictionary import: merge, preserving non-matches
workflow: Developer imports each artifact type through the same wizard shape, with the merge-vs-replace behavior depending on the specific artifact.
relevance: Confirms the already-captured atomic-install and merge-vs-replace principles; none of these specific artifact types (themes, plug-ins as separate installable units, schema-driven UI Defaults) exist as distinct concepts in Paddock Developer.
skip_for_web: Artifact types don't map; underlying atomicity principle already captured elsewhere.

name: Importing an Application Blueprint (Markdown Spec-Driven Development)
apex: APEX accepts a Markdown-based 'blueprint' file describing what an application should do, what the database means, and how users work with the data; an AI assistant turns that spec into an inspectable, reviewable application design artifact before the real application is created, importable with a chosen Generative AI Service, Parsing Schema, and Application ID.
attributes: spec as durable source of truth
workflow: Developer or AI assistant writes a Markdown spec, imports it as a Blueprint, picks an AI service and schema, and reviews the AI-generated application design before it becomes a real application.
relevance: This is an application-creation feature (spec-driven scaffolding), already covered conceptually by run 6's 'creating an application using spec-driven development' entry; the deploying chapter's Import page just adds a second entry point to the same feature, not a new concept for the designer.
skip_for_web: Already assessed under application-creation, not deployment.

name: Exporting and Importing from App Builder (chapter overview)
apex: Table-of-contents page introducing the export/import chapter: Understanding the Export and Import Process, Creating Export Files, Importing Export Files, and Managing Export Files from the Export Repository.
relevance: Pure navigation page; its children are each assessed individually elsewhere in this batch.
skip_for_web: No unique content.

name: Creating Export Files (chapter overview)
apex: Table-of-contents page listing every export sub-type covered in this batch: splitting files, static files, application, page, components, themes, plug-ins, UI Defaults, feedback, REST Source Catalog, workspace, and script repository.
relevance: Pure navigation page; each listed sub-topic is assessed individually elsewhere in this batch.
skip_for_web: No unique content.

name: Export Repository (staged uploads: install later or delete)
apex: A durable staging list (under Utilities > Export Repository) holding every uploaded export file, whether installed immediately or not; each row can be Installed on demand (Action column, replaying the same install wizard) or removed via Delete Checked.
attributes: install later from SQLcl as an alternative
workflow: Developer uploads a file once, then decides later whether to install it, re-attempt a failed install, or discard it, without re-uploading.
relevance: Good staging-area pattern for a future Paddock import/apply-from-git-branch flow: separate 'receive an incoming change' from 'apply it', keeping a reviewable list of pending artifacts an admin can install or discard on their own schedule.
skip_for_web: Skip the SQLcl install path; keep the receive-then-install-on-demand separation.

name: How to Create a Custom Application (Supporting Objects: bundled DB objects + install/upgrade/deinstall scripts)
apex: A 'Supporting Objects' feature that bundles an application's required database objects, seed data, and static files into version-locked Installation, Upgrade, and Deinstallation script sets (with pre-installation validations, sanitized HTML install/upgrade/deinstall messages, prompted substitution strings and build options), so end users deploy a self-contained distributable app in a single guided wizard instead of manual multi-step setup.
workflow: Developer authors install/upgrade/deinstall scripts once; anyone importing the app gets a guided wizard offering to run them immediately or later.
relevance: This targets building a redistributable packaged product installed independently by many third parties on their own instances; Paddock is one continuously-deployed site, and Prod Supabase writes explicitly require the operator to name the action rather than run through an automated installer wizard.
skip_for_web: The whole redistributable-package model conflicts with Paddock's manual-infra-write policy.

name: Install Summary (session-scoped install/deinstall log)
apex: A log viewable from the Supporting Objects Tasks list showing results of the most recent installation or deinstallation, but only for the current APEX session (not a persistent history).
workflow: Developer checks Install Summary right after running an install/upgrade/deinstall to see what happened.
relevance: Session-scoped-only logging is a weaker pattern than Paddock's own Data workspace, which already keeps a persistent loader-run history; nothing to copy here.
skip_for_web: Inferior to the existing Data workspace design.

name: About Publishing an Application URL (Friendly URL and f?p syntax)
apex: Explains how to find and share a production application URL, decomposing both Friendly URL syntax (server/path-prefix/app-alias/page-alias) and legacy f?p syntax (app id/page/session), and warns never to share a URL containing a live session ID since it is per-user and will error for anyone else.
attributes: session ID (never share in a URL)
workflow: Developer finds the app's Run link, strips any session-id suffix, and shares the clean alias-based URL publicly.
relevance: Generic URL-sharing hygiene (don't leak a session token in a shared link) that Paddock's cookie-based Clerk sessions already avoid by construction; the alias/routing syntax itself was already covered in an earlier run's URL-syntax topic.
skip_for_web: Session-in-URL is not how Paddock's auth works.

name: Build Options (named Include/Exclude feature flags on any component)
apex: A reusable, named flag with exactly two states (Include/Exclude) that can be attached to a page, region, page control, or shared component via its Configuration property; when Excluded, APEX treats the tagged item as if it did not exist at runtime. Applying one is done in Page Designer's Property Editor, and can be toggled directly from the Rendering-tab context menu once applied (this is the mechanism behind the earlier Comment Out/Uncomment debugging feature).
attributes: Build Options page (Shared Components > Application Logic)
workflow: Developer defines a named flag once, tags any number of components with it via one property, then flips the single flag to turn all tagged components on or off together.
relevance: A strong candidate general-purpose primitive for Paddock Developer: a named on/off flag attachable to any component's settings, so multiple regions/pages can be grouped under one toggle (e.g. 'winter break mode', 'experimental widget') without editing each one individually.
skip_for_web: None; this fits directly into the 'general components in a designer' goal.

name: Deleting Build Options and Associated Components (Utilization safety net)
apex: A build option's Create/Edit page lists its Associated Components at the bottom; deleting a build option does NOT delete those components (they simply stop being gated), so Oracle recommends reviewing Associated Components first, with a separate explicit 'Remove Components' action (with confirmation) if the components themselves should also be deleted. A Utilization report (once any build option exists) and a History report show where each flag is used and how it has changed.
attributes: Associated Components list on the flag's edit page
Delete (removes only the flag, not its components)
workflow: Developer checks Associated Components/Utilization before deleting a flag, and explicitly opts in to also removing the components if that's really the intent.
relevance: Good safety pattern to copy for any shared/reusable primitive in Paddock Developer (flags, Lists, Component Settings): show a 'where is this used' report before deletion, and make deleting the container distinct from deleting what it contains.
skip_for_web: None.

name: Viewing Build Option Reports (Utilization and History)
apex: Two reports on the Build Options page once at least one flag exists: Utilization shows where a selected build option is referenced across the current application; History shows what modifications have been made to build options over time.
attributes: Utilization tab (appears only after a build option exists)
workflow: Developer picks a flag in the Utilization report to see everywhere it gates, or opens History to audit past changes to flags.
relevance: Confirms the 'where is this used' + 'what changed and when' report pair is standard practice for any shared/reusable primitive; both are worth building for Paddock's own flags, Lists, and Component Settings.
skip_for_web: None.

name: Selecting a Build Option (applying a flag via Property Editor)
apex: Applying an already-created build option to a page, region, page control, or shared component is done through the Configuration group in Page Designer's Property Editor, after which it can be toggled from the Rendering-tab context menu.
workflow: Developer selects a component in the designer tree, opens its Configuration properties, and assigns an existing named flag to it.
relevance: Confirms the flag-assignment UX sits in the same Configuration property group as other component settings, which is the natural place for Paddock Developer to expose an equivalent 'flag' field on any component's settings panel.
skip_for_web: None; reinforces the previous Build Options finding rather than adding new ground.

name: Exporting Build Options or Build Option Status (flag-only deploy, dark launch pattern)
apex: A dedicated Build Options Status export lets a developer ship a feature disabled in production (its components tagged EXCLUDE) and later turn it on by exporting and applying only the changed flag statuses (EXCLUDE to INCLUDE), without re-exporting or redeploying the feature's actual components.
attributes: Component Export > Build Options Status tab
workflow: Developer deploys a hidden feature dark (flag=Exclude), then later flips the flag to Include and exports/applies just that status change to make the feature go live instantly.
relevance: This is the textbook dark-launch feature-flag pattern: ship code disabled, flip a small, independent flag-only artifact to activate it later without a full redeploy. Worth designing Paddock's own flag primitive so its on/off state can be changed and applied independently of a full page/component export.
skip_for_web: Skip the ZIP/translation export mechanics; keep the decouple-flag-state-from-content-deploy principle.

name: One-Click Remote Application Deployment
apex: Deploys an application directly to a remote APEX instance over a REST Enabled SQL Service connection (Basic/Schema/OAuth2 Client Credentials auth), reusing the same export-scope options (Supporting Objects, Public/Private Reports, Comments, Translations) plus deployment overrides (target schema/workspace, overwrite-existing toggle, application ID/alias override); Oracle recommends using 'empty credentials' in shared dev environments so the client ID/secret must be typed at the moment of each deploy, ensuring only someone who actually knows them can trigger a remote deploy.
workflow: Developer picks or creates a remote deployment target, supplies credentials (or leaves them empty to be prompted each time), sets export scope and overwrite behavior, and clicks Deploy to push the app straight to the remote instance.
relevance: Paddock's deploy step is already a git merge to main triggering Cloudflare Workers Builds automatically; a manual one-click-deploy button in the designer would duplicate that pipeline. The one transferable idea is requiring a human to supply credentials at the moment of a high-privilege action rather than having them stored and silently reusable, which echoes Paddock's existing 'name the action' rule for prod Supabase writes.
skip_for_web: Whole feature is superseded by the existing CI/CD pipeline; only the human-must-confirm-at-the-moment security principle is worth remembering, and it is already policy.

name: Legacy Forms Optimized for Mobile Environments (List View, Column Toggle, Reflow Report)
apex: Three deprecated-but-still-supported mobile-responsive report region types that predate Interactive Grid/Report's own responsive views: List View (card-like rows for phones), Column Toggle (end users pick visible columns via a Columns button, with a per-column numeric priority controlling which hide first at narrow widths), and Reflow Report (collapses columns into vertical label/value pairs when the viewport is too narrow). Oracle explicitly says not to use them for new development.
attributes: Column Toggle region (Columns button, column priority)
supported column types: Plain Text, Link, Percent Graph, etc.
workflow: Developer would add one of these region types from the Gallery and bind it to a SQL query, but only for maintaining old applications.
relevance: Explicitly deprecated by Oracle itself and superseded by Interactive Grid/Report's built-in icon/detail responsive views (already captured in an earlier run); Paddock's Tailwind-based responsive layouts already solve narrow-viewport tables without needing a dedicated legacy component.
skip_for_web: The whole chapter is 'still works, don't use it' guidance with a modern in-house replacement Paddock already has an equivalent of.

name: Viewing Legacy Components in the Gallery (hidden-by-default deprecated components)
apex: Deprecated/legacy component types are hidden from Page Designer's component Gallery by default; a developer must explicitly choose Gallery Menu > Show Legacy Components to reveal them.
workflow: Developer toggles a menu option only when they specifically need to add or inspect a deprecated component type.
relevance: Simple, reusable pattern worth adopting as Paddock Developer's component library evolves: default-hide superseded component types from the 'add component' picker rather than deleting them outright, with an explicit opt-in reveal for existing usages.
skip_for_web: None; small but directly applicable UX idea.

name: Deployment Scenarios to Consider (workspace/schema/database combinations + never hard-code the app ID)
apex: Four export/import deployment topologies (same workspace+schema; different workspace, same schema; different workspace+schema; different database entirely), plus guidance on whether to copy the workspace (needed for APEX-authentication user migration) or database (schema name is irrelevant, can be renamed on import), and a strong recommendation to never hard-code an application ID, instead using the application alias or APP_ID/APP_ALIAS substitution strings.
workflow: Developer picks the narrowest topology that satisfies isolation needs, and always references the running app by alias/substitution string rather than a hard-coded numeric ID.
relevance: Paddock's git-branch-to-Worker topology already replaces this whole decision tree; the never-hard-code-an-identifier principle is already followed via environment variables and config.
skip_for_web: Topology options are specific to APEX's export/import deployment model.

name: Supporting Object Definitions export option (bundling schema DDL + seed data with an app export)
apex: A Custom Export option (Yes / No / Yes and Install on Import Automatically) that encapsulates an application's required database object definitions, image definitions, and seed data SQL into the same single export file as the application metadata, optionally auto-installing them on command-line import.
attributes: Supporting Object Definitions: Yes and Install on Import Automatically (CLI only)
workflow: Developer bundles the schema/seed-data a page depends on into the same export so a target environment can be stood up in one step instead of running migrations separately.
relevance: Relevant question for Paddock's weekly git export to consider explicitly: whether a design export should snapshot/reference the Supabase schema/migration it depends on, or deliberately stay silent on schema and leave that to the existing manual, operator-named migration process.
skip_for_web: Skip the auto-install-on-CLI-import mechanic, which conflicts with Paddock's manual-infra-write policy; keep the bundling question as something to decide deliberately rather than by default.

name: Server-side APEX_DEBUG API vs client-side apex.debug API (two instrumentation surfaces feeding one log)
apex: APEX_DEBUG's PL/SQL procedures run on the server and write to the shared debug log; apex.debug is the separate client-side JavaScript equivalent, printing to the browser developer console only when the session's debug level is active, so Dynamic-Action JS code can be instrumented the same way as server code.
attributes: gated by the same session/instance debug level
workflow: Developer adds apex.debug(...) calls inside client-side JavaScript (e.g. Dynamic Action code) so those messages only appear in the browser console when debug mode is active, mirroring how APEX_DEBUG works on the server.
relevance: Paddock's Debug panel spans both a server (Worker) and a client (browser) runtime, so it needs two matching instrumentation helpers gated by the same on/off switch, not just a server-side logger; apex.debug is the concrete model for the client half.
skip_for_web: None; this is a needed second half of the debug-instrumentation finding already noted for the server side.

name: Server-side Condition = Never (alternative, destructive way to disable a component)
apex: Setting a component's Server-side Condition Type to Never prevents it from rendering or executing, as an alternative to Comment Out; Oracle warns this destroys any existing condition the component already had, so it recommends the Build-Option-backed Commented Out flag instead for temporary isolation.
attributes: Property Editor > Server-side Condition > Type: Never
workflow: Developer sets a component's condition to Never to force it off, understanding this is a one-way overwrite of whatever condition logic was already there.
relevance: Explicitly the worse of the two options per Oracle's own guidance (destructive vs. the non-destructive Comment Out flag already flagged as the pattern worth copying); recorded only as the cautionary contrast.
skip_for_web: Superseded by the Comment Out/Uncomment pattern already captured as the recommended approach.

name: Include Installation Files toggle for version control (exclude boilerplate scaffold files)
apex: A Component Export's ZIP option to leave out the generated install.sql/set_environment.sql/end_environment.sql scaffold files entirely, recommended specifically when saving to version control so an application's shared installation files are not repeatedly overwritten by every unrelated component export.
attributes: Include Installation Files: On (adds install.sql, set_environment.sql, end_environment.sql)
Include Installation Files: Off (recommended for VCS)
workflow: Developer turns Include Installation Files off before committing a component export to git so only the component's own content file changes, not shared boilerplate.
relevance: Reinforces a concrete git-hygiene rule for Paddock's weekly export: any generated wrapper/index/manifest file that is common to many components should be excluded or kept stable so it does not churn the diff on every run.
skip_for_web: None.

name: Audit Information export scope (None / Names and Dates / Dates Only)
apex: A recurring export field across nearly every export type (application, page, components, themes, plug-ins, feedback, REST catalog) controlling whether Created/Changed By-User and On-Date metadata rides along, defaulting to None.
attributes: Audit Information: Dates Only (dates without user identity)
workflow: Developer chooses whether an export should carry authorship metadata, e.g. keeping dates for change-tracking while stripping usernames.
relevance: Worth deciding deliberately for Paddock's weekly git export: whether committed design files should carry any authorship/timestamp metadata beyond what git itself already records, and whether internal usernames should ever appear in a git-tracked export.
skip_for_web: None.

name: Pre-installation Validations and Prerequisites (guard rails before an install runs)
apex: Under Supporting Objects, Prerequisites define built-in environment checks (free disk space, required system privileges, schema object restrictions) and Pre-installation Validations define custom business-rule checks, similar to page validations, that block an install entirely if user-defined conditions are not met.
attributes: Prerequisites (free disk space, system privileges, schema restrictions)
workflow: Developer defines checks that must pass before an install proceeds, so a misconfigured target environment is rejected up front instead of failing mid-install.
relevance: Reinforces the atomic-and-validated theme already found in the import chapter: any future Paddock apply/import-from-git-branch action should validate preconditions up front and refuse to start rather than fail partway through.
skip_for_web: Skip the disk-space/system-privilege specifics (no analog in a Worker runtime); keep the validate-before-starting principle.

name: Application Substitution Strings (static reusable text tokens, promptable at install time)
apex: Named static substitution strings for phrases or labels reused in many places across an application; when packaging a custom application, the installer can prompt the person installing it to fill in values for specific substitution strings at install time.
attributes: install-time prompt for a substitution string value
workflow: Developer defines a token once (e.g. a company name or tagline used across many pages) and references it everywhere instead of repeating literal text; a packaged installer can ask the installer to customize it.
relevance: A simpler, non-translation sibling to Text Messages worth knowing about, but Paddock's config/content system (content/ files, env vars) already covers reusable site-wide values without needing a dedicated substitution-string registry.
skip_for_web: Install-time prompting is specific to APEX's redistributable-package model, already judged not applicable.
